XenotypeDef.label: bloodfiend
XenotypeDef.description:
Bloodfiends are a type of xenohuman transformed by a mysterious, archite-suppressed, bloodborne illness. Touted as a curse by ancient Coreworld myths, "Dipsia" is a condition characterized by its rapid mutation of a host into a haematophagic apex predator. While visually indistinguishable from other xenohumans, save for notable blood red eyes, Bloodfiends are biologically immortal, significantly stronger, more agile and resistant than any ordinary person. Foregoing standard metabolic systems, Bloodfiends are fuelled by the fresh blood of other xenohumans. A properly fed Bloodfiend is even stronger, nigh-unkillable, capable of healing from otherwise permanent wounds and can exert a certain degree of control over the archites in their bloodstream to form crystalline Hardblood: a strong, versatile material that can be molded for defensive or offensive purposes. Bloodfiends possess a natural, nearly debilitating phobia of water.
Bloodfiends, despite their nature, are highly intelligent and generally civilized. Their societies are structured in strict genealogical hierarchies: Dipsia dillutes through generations of a bloodline, propagating via xenogerm implantation and blood transfusions. First Kindreds present the highest possible ratio of Dipsia to suppressant archites possible, while an Eighth Kindred's Dipsia concentration would be so weak in relation to the same archites that their powers are greatly diminished. The weaker kindred answer to the stronger as superiors and possess an instinctual aversion to disobedience .
For centuries, myths surrounding Bloodfiends touted fire as a ward against them. This has been scientifically proven as fact. Due to its complex nature, Bloodfiend regeneration has a difficult time reconstituting burnt tissue. Being actively on fire rapidly drains a Bloodfiend's hemogen supply as their regeneration attempts to keep up with a constant source of damage.
Dipsia itself has been a rumored and recorded phenomenon throughout most human history.
Recent breakthroughs in analysis and exploration of archotech vestige facilities have revealed that they possessed knowledge of the condition. Bloodfiends that distinguish themselves from their feral Bloodbag counterparts were found to possess suppressant archites developed to contain the worst of the illness' mutagenic properties, though proved generally insufficient at stopping the condition from progressing.
